analysis: The code snippet normalizes a resource path string. It calls substring twice: first with a single argument 1 inside a while loop that fires only if the string starts with "//", ensuring at least 2 characters so index 1 is valid; second with arguments (0, length-1) inside a while loop that fires only if the string ends with "/", ensuring at least 1 character so the indices are valid. The string is trimmed first, so empty strings (after trimming) bypass both loops. Both calls are safely guarded by loop conditions, preventing any IndexOutOfBoundsException.
answer: The only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException. Its throwing conditions (negative beginIndex, endIndex larger than length, beginIndex > endIndex) are fully avoided by the loop guards and the nature of the operations.
remark: The substring calls are always made when the string length is sufficient (at least 2 for the first, at least 1 for the second) due to the while loop conditions. Therefore, IndexOutOfBoundsException cannot occur under any input.
